review.review:
I used to say that MW19 was the last good COD (Multiplayer wise) but after buying this game on a good discount my opinion has changed and I think this is honestly the last good COD Multiplayer they've made. Sure it's pretty much a 70 dollar DLC (17 dollars in my case) for MWII but I'll take this over MW4 (jesus christ the MW4 beta was the worst multiplayer shooter experience I have ever played it's literally a BO6 DLC without the omnimovement or whatever that bs is called).

No I will not talk about the Campaign I stopped caring about COD Campaigns since Ghosts and I'd rather not waste 3 hours (pretty much the length of the campaign) of my life playing another COD boring campaign. 

Zombies? Yea I tried playing Zombies but instead I fell asleep because it's the most boring zombies experience I've played that I think BO1 on the DS zombies is more enjoyable.

Now the most important part of this review, Multiplayer. Lots of game modes and playlists to play it's nice to see this game has a plentiful variety of game modes after they stopped caring about this game. There is also a crazy amount of maps including reimagining of the MW2 2009 maps but the ones I really despise the most are the cel shaded ones like tf I thought this was COD not Fortnite? Oh and most importantly not every map is the size of a post it stamp *looking at BO6*. There is so many freaking guns you can choose while most of the guns in this game are borrowed from MWII but besides the MWII guns there's a good amount of new ones though. Can't forget how much customization for your guns this game has to offer. If you're looking for a decent COD Multiplayer definitely get this one it's worth it on sale don't buy full price tho. If buying for Campaign/Zombies don't even bother.

review.review:
Game is solid, I have a lot to say about the game. before I start though, this review is negative because this game feels like crap to run. I have a 6800XT and I get crashes from time to time along with alot of random stuttering. Luckily the issue isnt nearly as bad as it was in Cold War for me.

The Good: I do enjoy the gunplay for this game, it feels very fluid which also works against itself in some ways. Lots of camos to pick even if some are just unobtainable now, so there is a lot of gun customization. I do enjoy that you can just get any weapon from DMZ, but it eliminates the natural progression of unlocks that have been around since CoD 4. Last good thing is that I personally do like the maps that come from MW(2019) up to this game, not much of a praise IMHO.

The Bad: 
Multiplayer:
There is a lot of bad just being honest. SBMM is a disaster, I understand that cod should be more all inclusive and that there are certain brackets for certain players (this is why ranked play existed). But why does every match have to feel like a sweat-fest. By no means am I bad at this game (i have dropped a nuke before), but every match I play when I try to level guns and unlock just stuff, I have to go against people who are max rank using some meta choice and never bother trying anything else. 

Gunsmith feels pointless, besides the Jak conversions which are a really cool idea. What I mean is there are so many attachments ingame, but every single build based on best attachments for stats use the same muzzles, sights, lasers, foregrips, and grips (any version of an AK for example), so ~30-40 attachments out of hundreds (including duplicates due to some weapon types requiring you to re-unlock the same muzzle/foregrip).

The available maps make me question my sanity. From what I can recall from 2008-2012, NOBODY wants to play Derail, these old MW2 original maps do not mesh well with this game at all. I loved Wasteland, Karachi and Favela back then but I struggle to find people like im playing CoD Ghosts again all these years later. Some maps do make a return but only in DMZ which came from Warzone, for instance Sub Base from MW2 and Seatown from MW3, both being great maps.

Lastly, weapon balancing: I know it is a CoD staple to argue over how powerful different weapon archetypes are, "snipers are too fast", "shotguns have too much range", etc. This game definitely prioritizes automatic firearms, in fact it made SMGs more powerful than a good 70% of the game's other weapon choices. Added to that, this game added MW2 weapons and operators to this game which is nice ,but all MW3 guns are widely considered better than the MW2 weapons.

DMZ:
DMZ feels like a shell of its past self, there isn't much to do besides go into the Dark Aether and just generally mess around in tier 3 while trying to complete campaign missions to unlock new recipes. Feels like a waste of time compared to older zombies besides. Another thing, trying to do any steps to unlock Dark Aether sigils before getting access to print scorcher cases is torture. It is an actual uphill battle if >3 people rush tier 3 with scorches at the start of the match. Last thing about DMZ, just like before- if steam servers go down, your game randomly crashes, or you disconnect from the match randomly. ALL OF YOUR OPERATOR GEAR VANISHES. I can't count on two hands how much one of these three things has happened to either me or a friend and made us waste another match hunting down gear again

Campaign is just not it, pretty well known. I don't really have much to add.

There is a bunch more negative stuff but I would be yapping too long beyond this review. Stuff like how recoil means nothing anymore, and how the slower TTK doesn't feel as good. I'll just end it off here.

**Modern Warfare III is a mixed bag for me.**

I mainly play COD for the **campaign and Zombies** because I don’t even bother with multiplayer anymore. The amount of hackers and cheaters completely kills the experience for me, and I have no interest in sweating through matches wondering whether someone is actually good or just cheating.

The campaign has some genuinely cool moments, great characters, and solid gunplay, but overall it feels **too short and rushed**. A lot of the open-combat missions just don’t hit the same as the classic cinematic COD missions. For a Modern Warfare game, I expected a much stronger story experience.

Zombies can be fun, and the core shooting still feels great, but the game as a whole feels like it could have been so much better with more effort put into the campaign and stronger action against cheaters.

**Good gunplay, disappointing campaign length, and multiplayer ruined by hackers.**

**I still enjoy parts of MWIII, but it definitely isn’t the Modern Warfare experience I was hoping for.**

review.review:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III is a game I have mixed feelings about. There are definitely things I enjoyed, especially the multiplayer, but overall it feels like it could have been much better.

The gunplay is still really satisfying, and bringing back classic maps was a great idea. Some of the old maps work surprisingly well with the newer movement and mechanics, and the faster gameplay makes matches feel intense.

The Zombies mode is also a nice addition, especially if you enjoy playing with friends. Having a big open map and completing contracts while fighting hordes of zombies can be pretty addictive.

Unfortunately, the campaign is where the game really disappointed me. Some missions feel rushed, and the whole campaign doesn't have the same impact as Modern Warfare 2019 or even MWII. It feels like there was potential for a much better story.

The multiplayer can also be frustrating, especially with matchmaking and balancing. Some matches feel like you're fighting for your life just to get a positive K/D. 😂

Overall, MWIII isn't a terrible game, but it feels more like an expansion that was turned into a full release. **Good gunplay, fun multiplayer and Zombies, but a disappointing campaign and some questionable decisions.** 🔥🎖️

Today, the glamour of single-player campaigns is obscured by co-op and online meaningless gaming.
A good story in a game is, for me, better than a movie. At least in a game I have a part in the movie, although it always has a script.
I've been gaming for more than 40 years and the first Modern Warfare story was a glory walk to a grand finale.
This remake is more modern and less cruel and raw than the first one.

Before, when CoD had the competition of Battlefield in single-player campaigns, both software houses produced some of the most incredible stories I've ever played. Structure, motive, action... it kept the gamer in a kind of stasis and, when the story was cut by the finale of each episode, it kept us starving for more... and more. It hooked you to the game.

Now, senseless multiplayer and pay-to-win rule the gaming industry, where campaigns are just a small part of the investment and the stories are empty most of the time.

Multiplayer gaming is now full of idiotic cheaters that ruin the experience of any gamer, full of dollar-wide upgrades and skins that really mean nothing.

Fortunately, CoD's single-player campaign is still good and entertaining. Along with some other FPS games like Cyberpunk, the industry is still making good products, but they are becoming scarce, as the new generations prefer to show off in multiplayer like peacocks rather than immersing themselves in a good fantasy.
It is easier to play 20 minutes with a shiny skin and a paid-to-win upgrade... completing a game story is like reading a book: it takes time and dedication to get to the end of it.

Though this MW III story is clearly not the best and not the longest, it at least captured the thrill and the action needed for war games like this.
Modern Warfare games are a dystopian future where madness takes over the world so that chaos can reign.

If you fail to understand that this has a moral behind it and you just want to play with other players online, then CoD's soul will die and you will have an empty shell without purpose.

Keep investing in the stories. The youth needs fantasy in their minds and dreams in their sleep.

Also known as: 'the one with no offline, anything' - no offline campaign, no offline Zombies, no offline multiplayer. Yup, even botmatch is hosted on Activision's servers, and since the Zombies mode is a 'many player public instance' Warzone/DMZ derivative, you can't start that solo, either.

So in short, this is a zero longevity or preservation title. Plus, the campaign is pretty naff compared to the other Modern Warfare ones, too.

Why would I recommend it then? Seems pretty dumb if the game comes with a finite playtime attached to it.

Simply put, this has the best 'modern' Modern Warfare multiplayer available. Sledgehammer fixed everything that Infinity Ward got wrong with both MW'19 and MWII, while iterating on much of what makes Treyarch's multiplayer so compelling, too. Add to that, an insane amount of seasonal content and unlocks, and you've got a mountain of a game to climb. All crafted while fully maintaining the original MW franchise aesthetic and style.

It still has the Warzone-era SBMM, but with no stats tracking left in the game to sweat over, and a gazillion and one things to unlock, try, and work towards, there's zero reason to stress. Just go into each game with a plan - tinker with this, unlock that, do this skin, or whatever - and blank the end score result.

You'll still get the shooty-bang fix, only without the aneurysm that usually accompanies it.

Definitely one to catch when it's on sale. The best of the 'modern' MW brand game, and the high bar that IW are unlikely to ever match Sledge at.

Really looking forward to seeing whatever it will be that Sledgehammer servers up next, presuming M$ don't sack everything before its launch year.

review.review:
Rating: 👎 Not Recommended
Hours Played: Enough to question my life choices.

The Campaign: Honestly... Not Bad?
Look, credit where it's due. The campaign is actually decent. It’s exactly what you want from a Call of Duty story: loud noises, kicking down doors, and doing sneaky stuff in the dark. It’s like a solid action movie you watch on a lazy Sunday. If the game was just this, I’d probably leave a thumbs up.

The Multiplayer: Welcome to the Sweat Lodge
This is where the dream dies. I don't know what happened to casual matchmaking, but every single person in my lobby is playing like their family is being held hostage and the only way to save them is to drop-shot me.

I bought a rig with an RTX 5070 and a crisp 2K 165Hz display, and for what? Just so I can watch my K/D ratio plummet in ultra-smooth, crystal-clear high definition. I even spent 45 minutes calibrating the stick deadzones and response curves on my GameSir controller, thinking I was about to go pro. I spawned in and was immediately 360-slide-canceled into oblivion by a 14-year-old wearing a giant glowing rat costume.

Spawns: I spawn, I take one step, I get shot in the back. I spawn again, I throw a grenade, I die to my own grenade because someone shot it out of the air.

SBMM (Skill-Based Matchmaking): I had one good game where I went 15-10. The game immediately decided I was ready to compete in the CDL Grand Finals against a team of movement demons who haven't seen sunlight since 2023.

Final Verdict:
Play the campaign, pat yourself on the back, and then uninstall. If you hate yourself and enjoy high blood pressure, load up the multiplayer.

review.review: THE BEST SHOOTER GAME NOT BORING AT ALL! They still aren't fully developed years later and they keep making games when they shouldn't. I don't get it. I mean, look at other titles like Battlefield, they manage to innovate all the time. Seems like the player base is getting smaller and smaller, doesn’t it? Call of Duty keeps cranking out new installments every few years. But I love this game, it has that addictive CoD DNA! But like, if you're gonna put out a new title every couple years, at least make it really different than the last one. Otherwise it just gets cringey. The multiplayer is really amazing – the movement is really tight and frenetic – but honestly, it seems like they are reusing maps from MW2. And don't even get me started on Zombies. The DMZ extraction style is a decent attempt at keeping things interesting instead of just running rounds but it still feels like glorified content meant just to push us into unlocking more guns for MP. If you can't innovate on the core gameplay loop or the maps then what are we really paying for? Now it’s nostalgia bashing! What I really love is how CoD really leans into being an arcade shooter rather than a tactical one like CS2. Those competitive games require absolute precision and meticulous team strategy, which is great in its own way, but CoD is all about the sheer fun. It’s much more about personal skill cutting through the massive explosions and constant action, which makes it feel less like a rigid esports simulation and more like pure, exhilarating entertainment!

review.review:
With MW4 just hours away from launching, I bought MW3 because it was on sale for around $14 USD (Chilean price). Even though I didn't play it right at launch—since I wasn't convinced by it—I’m left with mixed feelings now.
I thought the campaign would be shorter, as people claimed, but it didn't really feel that way to me.
I liked that they adopted the tactical aiming mechanics found in other games of this genre.
The downsides:
They really messed up by adding *Fortnite*-style skins to the multiplayer.
They could have added more weapons instead of just reusing the ones from MW2 with only a few extras.
In short:
I give the game an 8/10; it offers gameplay variety across the campaign, Zombies mode, and multiplayer, making it great for having fun for a while.
As a veteran player who has been around since *CoD 3*, I’d give it a 6/10—specifically because I miss the essence of the early days, which focused on the military theme rather than being so commercialized with all these microtransactions.
See you in MW4, everyone.

ESPAÑOL
A tan solo horas de que empiece a jugar el MW4, me compre el MW3 porque estaba en oferta prácticamente a unos 14 USD (precio Chile). Puedo decir que a pesar de no haber jugado el juego desde el inicio porque no le tenia fe, ahora puedo decir que me deja una sensación de agridulce.
Pensaba que la campaña duraba menos como decían pero siento que no fue tan así.
Me gusto que hayan copiado el apuntado táctico de otros juegos de este estilo  táctico.
Lo negativo:
La cagaron cuando pusieron skins tipo Fornite para el multijugador.
Pudieron agregar mas armas y no solo haber ocupado las del MW2 y poner un poco más.
En resumen:
El juego le doy un 8/10 el juego tiene variedad por jugabilidad en su campaña, modo zombie y multiplayer y para variedad sirve mucho para divertirse por un tiempo.
Para ser un jugador veterano desde el COD 3 le daría un 6/10 por la encencia desde sus inicios con el tema militar y no tan comercial con tantas micro transacciones
Nos vemos en el MW4 gente.
